Subject: Urgent: live ingest errors and throughput drop

Hi Kimberly,

We started seeing a sustained increase in 500/502 responses from the Redwood endpoint used for our live product recommendations around 14:30 PST today. Latency spiked from ~80ms to >1.2s and throughput dropped by ~40%. This is impacting personalization on our home page (traffic ~120k qps).

Attached are a short trace and a heap snapshot from our side. The errors look tied to many truncated streaming frames and a higher rate of parse exceptions in our client logs. We rolled back our recent client SDK bump and some errors reduced, but we're still seeing elevated error rates.

Can you please triage? We're sensitive to remediation timeline — we have a marketing campaign ramping tomorrow and can't take a further outage. If this needs exec attention, please escalate.

Thanks,
Claire Park
Head of Platform, Northstar Retail
claire.park@northstarretail.com

Forwarding Claire’s report and their traces. Key points:
- Sudden latency >1s and ~40% throughput loss.
- Client-side logs show truncated/fragmented frames and parse exceptions after we rolled to SDK v2.8.1.
- Rolling back client gave partial improvement per Claire.

Action request: can you triage streaming parser behavior and header/fragment reassembly logic? High priority — customer is in production with a major campaign. If you have an immediate mitigation we can push to them (server side flags or config). I’ve attached the logs Claire provided.

Thanks,
Kim

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 3 Feb 2026 16:05:50 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Urgent: live ingest errors and throughput drop

Triage notes (initial):
- Reproduced a similar parse exception locally by replaying their trace. The client SDK is emitting HTTP chunk boundaries that split header blocks in ways our streaming parser currently tolerates but then mis-merges when a subsequent small chunk arrives (edge-case with split headers + keep-alive).
- Root cause looks like a client SDK change to aggressive socket coalescing combined with our lenient header coalescer in the streaming path. Parser enters a transient state where KV cache gets out-of-sync and we see repeated retries + backpressure, which explains latency and throughput collapse.

Immediate mitigations:
1) Server-side strict-framing flag — we can flip this to reject split-header frames cleanly; client will fallback to non-streaming path (higher latency) but avoids parser corruption. Low-risk toggle, can be done in 15 minutes per pool.
2) Recommend Northstar rollback to SDK v2.8.0 (they already saw partial improvement).

Planned fix: patch streaming parser to validate header boundaries and reset parse state on malformed sequences. Target: non-blocking hotfix (0.1.1) within 48 hours, full regression suite + tests in 7 days.

I’ll prepare a short runbook for ops to flip strict-framing per region and will add a Jira (INF-9921). Sharing the replayed trace and stack snippets.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

Attachments: replayed-trace-namespace.log

Subject: Re: Urgent: live ingest errors and throughput drop

Claire — quick update: engineering identifies a client SDK + streaming parser interaction as the likely root cause. We can do two things immediately:

1) We can toggle a server-side strict-framing flag for your account/pool which will stop the malformed streaming reassembly and should restore throughput (expect a short window while connections drain). Dylan estimates this is low-risk and can be applied per-region.

2) We’ll prioritize a non-blocking hotfix to the parser (48h target for patch release). We’ll follow up with the regression test results within 7 days.

I’m also opening an SLA-exception request on your behalf to make sure any measurable impact to Feb billing is addressed — attaching the request. If you’re comfortable, we’d like to schedule an exec call this afternoon to walk through timeline and mitigation steps; Laura and Aditya will join. Please let me know a window that works.

Apologies for the disruption — we know the timing is bad with your campaign.

-Kim
